questionText:
Evaluate the definite integral:
$$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^{2} x}{\sin^{2} x + \cos^{2} x} \, dx$$

steps.title: Step 1: King's Property
steps.content: Using $\int_0^a f(x)dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)dx$, replace $x$ with $\pi/2 - x$.

steps.title: Step 2: Add Integrals
steps.content: Adding both integrals yields $2I = \int_0^{\pi/2} 1 \, dx = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies I = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

solution.shortcutMethod: Whenever $f(x) + f(a-x) = C$, the integral is strictly $\frac{a-0}{2} = \frac{\pi/2}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

questionText: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, then the matrix $A^{11}$ is equal to:

steps.title: Step 1: Mathematical Induction / Nilpotent Matrix
steps.content: Let $N = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$. Notice $N^2 = 0$.

steps.title: Step 2: Binomial Expansion
steps.content: Since $A = I + N$, $A^n = I + nN = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & n \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$. Here $n = 11$.

subject: maths
questionText: Find the value of $\lambda$ such that the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ are coplanar:

steps.title: Step 1: Condition for Coplanarity
steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.title: Step 2: Determinant Expansion
steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

subject: maths
questionText:
Evaluate the limit:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan x - \sin x}{x^3}$$

steps.title: Step 1: Trigonometric Factorization
steps.content: $\tan x - \sin x = \sin x \left(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\cos x}\right) = \tan x \cdot (1 - \cos x) = \tan x \cdot 2\sin^2(x/2)$.

steps.title: Step 2: Standard Limits
steps.content: $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \cdot \frac{2\sin^2(x/2)}{(x/2)^2 \cdot 4} = 1 \cdot \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questionText: Find the value of $\lambda$ such that the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ are coplanar:

steps.title: Step 1: Condition for Coplanarity
steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.title: Step 2: Determinant Expansion
steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

questionText:

$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan x - \sin x}{x^3}$$

steps.title: Step 1: Trigonometric Factorization

steps.title: Step 2: Standard Limits
steps.content: $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \cdot \frac{2\sin^2(x/2)}{(x/2)^2 \cdot 4} = 1 \cdot \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questionText: Find the value of $\lambda$ such that the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ are coplanar:

steps.title: Step 1: Condition for Coplanarity
steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.title: Step 2: Determinant Expansion
steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

questionText:
Evaluate the limit:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan x - \sin x}{x^3}$$

steps.title: Step 1: Trigonometric Factorization
steps.content: $\tan x - \sin x = \sin x \left(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\cos x}\right) = \tan x \cdot (1 - \cos x) = \tan x \cdot 2\sin^2(x/2)$.

steps.title: Step 2: Standard Limits
steps.content: $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \cdot \frac{2\sin^2(x/2)}{(x/2)^2 \cdot 4} = 1 \cdot \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

questionText:

questionText: Find the value of $\lambda$ such that the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ are coplanar:

steps.title: Step 1: Condition for Coplanarity
steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.title: Step 2: Determinant Expansion
steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

questionText:

$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan x - \sin x}{x^3}$$

steps.title: Step 1: Trigonometric Factorization

steps.title: Step 2: Standard Limits
steps.content: $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \cdot \frac{2\sin^2(x/2)}{(x/2)^2 \cdot 4} = 1 \cdot \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questionText: Find the value of $\lambda$ such that the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ are coplanar:

steps.title: Step 1: Condition for Coplanarity
steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.title: Step 2: Determinant Expansion
steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

questionText:
Evaluate the limit:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan x - \sin x}{x^3}$$

steps.title: Step 1: Trigonometric Factorization
steps.content: $\tan x - \sin x = \sin x \left(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\cos x}\right) = \tan x \cdot (1 - \cos x) = \tan x \cdot 2\sin^2(x/2)$.

steps.title: Step 2: Standard Limits
steps.content: $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \cdot \frac{2\sin^2(x/2)}{(x/2)^2 \cdot 4} = 1 \cdot \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questionText:

steps.title: Step 2: Add Integrals

steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

questionText: Find the value of $\lambda$ such that the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ are coplanar:

steps.title: Step 1: Condition for Coplanarity
steps.content: Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product $[\vec{a} \,\vec{b} \,\vec{c}] = 0$.

steps.title: Step 2: Determinant Expansion
steps.content: $\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & \lambda & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10 + 3\lambda) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(\lambda - 6) = 20 + 6\lambda + 14 + \lambda - 6 = 7\lambda + 28 = 0 \implies \lambda = -4$.

questionText:

$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan x - \sin x}{x^3}$$

steps.title: Step 1: Trigonometric Factorization

steps.title: Step 2: Standard Limits
steps.content: $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \cdot \frac{2\sin^2(x/2)}{(x/2)^2 \cdot 4} = 1 \cdot \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

steps.content: $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right) \cdot \frac{2\sin^2(x/2)}{(x/2)^2 \cdot 4} = 1 \cdot \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.
